evidence.excerpt: Despite decades of guidance from ISO and industry bodies, formal quality cost reporting remains uncommon in small and medium-sized enterprises. This paper reports findings from a structured survey of 38 electronics manufacturers and contract assemblers in Serbia conducted in 2017–2018. Questionnaire sections covered CoQ measurement practices, cost categorisation schemes used, reporting frequency, and integration with management accounting. Thirty-one percent of respondents collected any formalised quality cost data; of those, 83% tracked only visible failure and scrap costs and none systematically estimated hidden costs. Ordinal logistic regression on firm-level predictors found that ISO 9001 certification was positively associated with CoQ data collection (OR = 3.2, p < 0.05), whereas firm size and export orientation were not significant after controlling for certification status. Interviews with quality managers at six firms identified lack of accounting system integration and perceived measurement effort as the primary barriers. The paper concludes with a compact CoQ implementation roadmap calibrated to the resource constraints typical of Serbian electronics SMEs.
